properties.state: {"decision":"RE-OPENS the settled choice that a claim's region is COMPUTED from a seed and a depth rather than stored as a node list. The existing rule is deliberate and stated in the tool itself — 'the region is COMPUTED from seed+depth rather than stored as a node list, so it follows the design as it changes' — and its benefit is real: a stored list goes stale the moment the design moves, which is the failure a claim board exists to avoid. The question re-opened is whether that is the ONLY shape a claim may take, or the default one. PROPOSED SHAPE, from the reporter: allow a claim over an explicit node LIST or over a QUERY, alongside seed+depth. A query would keep the follows-the-design property that motivated the original choice, which is the reason to prefer it over a bare list. NOT YET DECIDED — recorded so the trade is visible rather than re-derived.","name":"OPEN — a claimed region is computed from seed+depth, and a cross-cutting duty is not a radius: does a claim also take a list?","rationale":"Because the cost is now measured rather than argued. dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff, 2026-08-08: their lane was 'cold-test the retrievability of nodes another session mined', spanning two unrelated slices — there is no seed whose depth-2 radius is that work. They claimed a representative node and put the truth in the `note`, which means claim_report's PROSE was right while its STRUCTURED answer was wrong for them. That is the specific failure mode a structured board is supposed to remove. THE STRONGER EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL, AND IT IS THREE FOR THREE: both prior workers on the same lane skipped claim_region entirely and kept a text file of document paths instead, because a flat list described their actual region better than the graph could. A tool losing to a text file is the same shape as the finding that drove the read-half increment — 'today a document BEATS the graph for making a decision, and that is a fair fight the graph loses'. Cross-cutting duties (audit, cold-validation, a sweep over everything of one kind) are a general category, not one team's oddity, and the radius cannot express any of them. Counter-argument to weigh before deciding: a claim is ADVISORY and never a lock, so the cost of a wrong region is a colleague misreading who holds what, not a corrupted write — which is an argument for keeping the mechanism simple. Against that: an advisory board whose structured field is routinely wrong is how a signal gets trained into being ignored, which is the same objection raised against permanently-live seat liveness.","status":"proposed"}
